diagrams.title: Two-wattmeter method and the neutral shift of an unbalanced star
diagrams.cap: Two wattmeters measure total power in any 3-wire system, and on a balanced load their difference gives the reactive power and the power factor. With no neutral wire an unbalanced star load's star point floats to V<sub>N</sub>′N = ΣV<sub>k</sub>Y<sub>k</sub>/ΣY<sub>k</sub>, which unbalances the load voltages.
diagrams.qq: Two wattmeters read 5 kW and 0. Power factor?

diagrams.title: Star connection phasors
diagrams.cap: Phase voltages 120° apart. Line voltage V<sub>RY</sub> = V<sub>R</sub> − V<sub>Y</sub> is √3 times larger and leads V<sub>R</sub> by 30°.
diagrams.qq: Phase voltage 230 V in star. Line voltage?

diagrams.title: Three-phase voltages (sequence R-Y-B)
diagrams.cap: Three equal sines 120° apart. v<sub>R</sub> + v<sub>Y</sub> + v<sub>B</sub> = 0 at every instant (balanced). Reversing any two phases reverses motor rotation.
diagrams.qq: Phase difference between R and Y?

diagrams.title: Delta connection current phasors
diagrams.cap: In delta, line current = difference of two phase currents: √3 times larger and 30° behind the phase current.
diagrams.qq: Phase current 10 A in delta. Line current?
